nodes.observable: controlled eventual committor versus stationary eventual delta
nodes.scope: Generation 4a, 160 kernels, eventual committor on the pair-event epoch kernel

nodes.scope: Generation 5 targeted T->P and P->P pairs, N=4, O=3, H=0

nodes.observable: aggregate passage versus state-resolved passage
nodes.scope: Generation 7 effect-matched controls

nodes.scope: Generation 7B two-level pair-face control, 30 target singletons

nodes.observable: interaction residual across motifs and directions
nodes.scope: Generation 5 interaction census
nodes.statement: The magnitude of a two-rule interaction residual depends on the representation and the source graph. It is not, by itself, a stable discriminator of higher-order structure.

nodes.observable: I(T0; class), I(T0; edge count), I(T0; class | edge count)
nodes.scope: checkpoint 1 of the pair-event clock
nodes.statement: At checkpoint 1, star and triangle carry only edge-count information: class information equals edge-count information and the shape term is 0. Path carries an extra shape term. For R06 path the split is 0.02798 class, 0.008801 edge, 0.01918 shape. For R01 path it is 0.01023, 0.001393, and 0.008838. The edge term agrees between path and star to about 1e-16.

nodes.observable: plug-in mutual information
nodes.scope: Generation 8A finite contingency tables, 16 replicates
nodes.statement: Under the uniform raw prior, the plug-in mutual information about the first other 3-edge destination is 0.0127 to 0.0702 nats. The largest cell is 0.0702 nats. Checkpoint plug-in class information stays near 0.12 nats through pair epoch 512.

nodes.observable: max minus min dense-minus-sparse across 16 raw triads

nodes.statement: Exact dense-minus-sparse context ranges over 512 pair epochs are at the floor for R00, R03, and R07. nodes.observable: fitted pair-face weights against the higher-order target
nodes.scope: Generation 7B
nodes.statement: The two-parameter pair-face representation that matches aggregate passage uses its two slots as one unconditional weight. It does not carry the higher-order selectivity.

nodes.observable: dense-minus-sparse class occupancy
nodes.scope: Generation 8 Rounds 0–2, N=4, O=3, H=0, horizon 512
nodes.statement: Mode B exploration finds a large finite-grade sparse/dense occupancy axis. On the S01 expression the four grades are ordered +0.0645, +0.0389, -0.0429, -0.0841 in dense minus sparse. Suppress moves pair epochs toward 4–6 edges. Favour moves them toward 0–2. Unconditional grades move the axis further than conditional grades.

nodes.observable: orbit quotient versus the 16 raw triads
nodes.scope: Generation 8A context repair
nodes.statement: Graph-only hidden-context quotienting is formally invalid for labelled rules. The wrong symmetry was real. On this palette it did not hide a large first-destination effect.

nodes.observable: dense-minus-sparse occupancy under exhaustive context
nodes.scope: Generation 8A, 6144 episodes, 16 raw triads, horizon 512
nodes.statement: Exhaustive raw-context starts preserve the edge-count axis. Copied dense-minus-sparse values include R03 +0.1728, R01 +0.0723, R04 +0.0691, R00 +0.0033, R02 -0.0711, R06 -0.0854, R07 -0.1448, and composite R05 +0.2378. The 3-edge layer stays near 0.314.

nodes.observable: plug-in minus permutation null, compared with the exact kernel
nodes.scope: Generation 8B calibration of the Generation 8A tables

First-destination permutation-null means are 0.03024 to 0.03127 nats. The largest plug-in cell, R03 star at 0.07021 nats, is a structural-zero system whose exact value is below 1e-10.

nodes.observable: I(initial raw triad; first other 3-edge class)
nodes.scope: A0 palette, exact pair-event epoch kernel, uniform raw triad

nodes.observable: I(initial triad; graph class at pair epoch k)
nodes.scope: A0 palette, pair-event checkpoints through 512
nodes.statement: Exact initial-context graph-class information is transient. The largest value is R06 path at checkpoint 1, 0.02798 nats. By checkpoint 32 the largest exact class value is about 1.29e-9 nats. By checkpoint 64 every exact class value is below 1e-10. The labelled pair mask decays on the same schedule. The plug-in figure near 0.12 to 0.14 nats through epoch 512 is not persistent information.

nodes.observable: I(current triad; next pair slot | full labelled pair mask)
nodes.scope: A0 palette, six pair propensities renormalised on the next event being a pair event
nodes.statement: The current triad carries exact local next-slot information only where the rule reads triadic state. Balanced full-mask CMI is at the floor for R00, R03, and R07. It is 0.009749 nats for R01, R02, and R04, 0.010413 for R05, and 0.023368 for R06. Stationary pair-event values are 0.012025, 0.013240, and 0.016895 on those same groups.

nodes.observable: I(current triad; next pair slot | graph class) / I(current triad; next pair slot | full mask)
nodes.scope: stationary pair-event weighting
nodes.statement: Replacing the full labelled pair mask by graph isomorphism class retains 0.661 of the stationary next-slot CMI for R01, R02, and R04, 0.710 for R05, and 0.443 for R06. The discarded fraction is labelled alignment. Information in the next graph class given the current graph class is about 0.001 to 0.0026 nats.

nodes.observable: comparison of I(T0; Pk) with I(Tk; next slot | Pk)
nodes.scope: H=0 grammar of Generations 8–8B
nodes.statement: Local higher-order dependence and long-lived initial-condition memory are distinct. The current triad can alter the next pair slot after the initial triad has been forgotten by the visible pair process.

nodes.observable: I(initial triad; class), I(initial triad; edge count), I(initial triad; class | edge count) at checkpoint 1
nodes.scope: pair-event epoch kernel, canonical 3-edge sources, uniform initial triad
nodes.statement: Checkpoint 1 is the law of the first pair event after zero or more triad-only toggles. On R01 path the epoch gives class information 0.010230532737 nats, edge-count information 0.001392555411 nats, and shape-given-edge 0.008837977327 nats. On R06 path the three values are 0.027980335340, 0.008801031906, and 0.019179303434 nats. Star and triangle carry the edge term only. Forcing the first full event to be a pair event raises the path class information to the full Jensen-Shannon value, 0.019497133059 nats for R01 and 0.046736889544 nats for R06.

nodes.observable: I(current triad; next pair slot | full pair mask)
nodes.scope: balanced weighting of R01, R02, R04, and R06
nodes.statement: An inactive single pair rule gives probability 1/6 on each of the six slots. An active rule with one slot multiplied by m gives that slot probability m/(m+5) and each other slot probability 1/(m+5). Half the pair masks are admissible and, on those masks, half the triads match the one-bit gate, so the balanced conditional mutual information is one half of the equal-weight Jensen-Shannon divergence of the two laws. At m=1/4 the value is 0.009748566529643857 nats. At m=4 it is 0.023368444772049440 nats. The enumeration gap is at most 1.114e-15.

nodes.observable: balanced current-slot CMI beside I(initial gate; pair mask) at epoch 64
nodes.scope: H=0 grammar, R01 and R06, balanced law versus pair epoch 64
nodes.statement: The balanced current-context slot information remains the closed-form value, 0.009748566529643857 nats for a strong-suppress rule and 0.023368444772049440 nats for R06, after the information that the initial gate still carries about the pair mask has fallen below 1e-10. The chain has forgotten which initial triad it came from. The triad bit now present continues to multiply one pair-slot weight.

nodes.observable: sign of balanced rule-induced edge drift against the sign of dense-minus-sparse occupancy
nodes.scope: W4 strong grades on the A0 palette, compared with the Generation 8 occupancy signs
nodes.statement: Suppressing a dissolution raises expected edge count, favouring a dissolution lowers it, and suppressing a formation lowers it. The reweighted slot is a dissolution that would have removed an edge, or a formation that would have added one, and the grade moves the probability of that slot. This is the local sign of the Generation 8 sparse/dense occupancy axis. Unconditional rules move the balanced mean by twice the one-gate conditional mean, because the gate no longer switches the rule off. The sign does not determine how much stationary mass sits on each edge-count layer.

nodes.observable: E[change in pair-edge count | pair mask, gate]
nodes.scope: pair-event edge-count drift on R00 through R07
nodes.statement: On an active strong-suppress dissolution the rule-induced expected edge change is (6-k)/21. On an active strong-favour dissolution it is (k-6)/9. On an active strong-suppress formation it is -k/21. The balanced means are +5/168 for R01 and for R04, -5/168 for R02, +5/84 for R03, -5/72 for R06, and -5/36 for R07. R05 has no one-rule closed form; its balanced induced mean is 0.09325397. The stationary pair-event average of the expected change is at most 3.3e-15 in absolute value. The mean drift does not determine the stationary occupancy.

nodes.observable: gate-bit memory, full-triad memory, and pair-mask information of the initial triad
nodes.scope: R00, R01, and R06; pair-event checkpoints 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64; uniform initial triad on each canonical source
nodes.statement: On R01 and on R06, exact propagation gives I(initial full triad; current pair mask) equal to I(initial gate bit; current pair mask) to about 1e-16 at the stored checkpoints. By pair epoch 64 both quantities are below 1e-10, and the probability that the current gate bit equals the initial gate bit is 1/2. On R00 the pair-mask information of the initial triad stays at the numerical floor at every checkpoint from 0 through 64, while the same unused gate coordinate still mixes from probability 1 to probability 1/2.

nodes.observable: total variation and balanced CMI of q_m against the uniform slot law
nodes.scope: one active pair slot, six-slot normalisation, W4 strong grades
nodes.statement: At m=1/4 the action slot has probability 1/21 and each other slot has probability 4/21. Total variation from the uniform six-slot law is 5/42. At m=4 the action slot has probability 4/9 and each other slot has probability 1/9. Total variation is 5/18. The ratio of those total variations is 7/3, which is also the ratio of the balanced informations' Jensen-Shannon terms and of the closed-form edge drifts. Five unweighted slots remain in the normalising total, so the reciprocal grades sit at different distances from uniformity.

nodes.observable: balanced slot CMI and stationary class mass
nodes.scope: balanced local law of R01, R02, and R04; stationary class masses of R01 and R04
nodes.statement: R01, R02, and R04 have the same balanced full-mask slot information. Each reweights one pair slot by 1/4, reads one binary triad gate, and is admissible on exactly 32 of the 64 pair masks. The shared value does not depend on form versus dissolve, on which slot is named, or on present versus absent. The labelled kernels of R02 and of R04 are conjugate to the labelled kernel of R01, with transition-probability gap 0. Neither map preserves isomorphism class. Stationary class masses of R01 and R04 still agree to a maximum absolute difference of 1.424e-15. That class-mass agreement is a measured stationary identity. It is not implied by the slot swap being a graph homomorphism.

nodes.observable: finding record
nodes.scope: coherence ledger, from Generation 8C onward
nodes.statement: A finding has several dimensions. Magnitude, robustness, persistence, explanatory reach, and structural role are not one strength score. A small or fragile phenomenon may be structurally essential. A large robust phenomenon may be mechanistically generic. Literal observations stay in the ledger, and later relations are what establish significance.

nodes.observable: choice of the next round
nodes.scope: programme method after Generation 8C; the geometry is inside the model
nodes.statement: After exploratory statistics identify a stable non-zero structure, search for a minimal mechanistic representation before expanding the experiment. Prefer a small exact causal geometry inside the explicit transition law over repeated measurement of the same effect.

nodes.observable: I(initial triad; graph class | edge count) at pair-event checkpoint 1
nodes.scope: R01 and R06 on the canonical star, path, and triangle
nodes.statement: On the canonical path the action slot of R01 and of R06 is the middle edge. Reweighting that slot moves probability between the 2-edge matching and the 2-edge path, which share an edge count. Star and triangle have no such split inside one edge count, so a gate that reweights one of their slots changes edge count without changing shape. Path topology is the converter from a one-slot bias into shape-given-edge information at the first pair event.

nodes.observable: I(current triad; next pair slot | graph class) / I(current triad; next pair slot | full mask)
nodes.scope: stationary and balanced pair-event weightings of R01 and R06
nodes.statement: Under stationary pair-event weighting, conditioning on graph isomorphism class retains 0.66077 of the full-mask slot information for R01, R02, and R04, and 0.44345 for R06. Under a uniform state weight the retained fractions are 0.48472 and 0.64704, so the favour rule keeps the larger fraction when occupancy is held fixed. Placing the R06 law on the R01 occupancy retains 0.82306; placing the R01 law on the R06 occupancy retains 0.30836. The stationary fraction gap follows the occupancy. The largest single-class losses include the 3-edge path class e3-deg2211-tri0-comp1, whose labelled masks do not all contain the action edge in the same topological position.

nodes.observable: balanced I(current triad; next pair slot | full pair mask)
nodes.scope: R05, balanced weighting, all 1024 states
nodes.statement: R05's balanced slot information is 0.010413087564075357 nats. It equals (1/4) JS(uniform, q_{1/4} on slot 2-3) + (1/4) JS(q_{1/4} on slot 0-1, q on both weighted slots). The three bits edge 0-1, edge 2-3, and the gate are sufficient for the local law. The companion edge changes the denominator when both weighted edges are present. This is a local normalisation interaction. It is a separate statement from the Generation 5 and Generation 6 committor interaction and from the Generation 8 occupancy residual.

nodes.observable: resulting edge count and graph isomorphism class
nodes.scope: six one-edge toggles from each canonical 3-edge source mask
nodes.statement: From the canonical star, and from the canonical triangle, every one-edge toggle with the same resulting edge count lands in one isomorphism class. From the canonical 3-edge path, dissolving an end edge lands in the 2-edge path e2-deg2110-tri0-comp2 and dissolving the middle edge lands in the 2-edge matching e2-deg1111-tri0-comp2. Forming a short chord lands in e4-deg3221-tri1-comp1 and forming the long chord lands in the 4-cycle e4-deg2222-tri0-comp1.

nodes.observable: exact six-slot pair-event law
nodes.scope: R01, R02, R04, and R06; all 1024 states; W4
nodes.statement: On each single conditional pair rule in the A0 palette, the six-slot pair-event law is uniform on every state except those where the action edge is admissible and the named triad bit matches. Those two bits and the fixed multiplier determine the law. The other eight bits do not. The one-bit conjunction of the two bits is a sufficient statistic for this local law. It is not a sufficient statistic for the later trajectory.

nodes.observable: local composition grammar
nodes.scope: two primitive one-gate T->P rules at N=4, H=0, W4 and general positive multipliers
nodes.statement: In the current multiplicative-weight DSL, constraints compose as additive features in event-logit space, and a system's local law is the softmax of its active features. What cardinality two adds over one gate is two-bit dependence through additive levels, multi-slot bias with a shared denominator, gate partitions, switched gate reading, and slot-gate XOR. It cannot add a gate-by-gate coefficient.

nodes.observable: full-event weight table against the unconditional comparator
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: A | G => m together with A | NOT G => m has the same full ten-slot weight table as the unconditional rule A => m on all 1024 states. All 16 equal-weight complementary systems are of this kind, and the face and non-face placements of the eliminated gate give the same labelled law. With unequal weights the gate partitions the action into two levels: all 48 such systems are a two-level gate law with three rows, which the DSL cannot write as one primitive rule.

nodes.observable: favour/suppress ratio of total variation, edge drift, and balanced conditional mutual information
nodes.scope: one active pair slot, six-slot normalisation, W4 strong grades m=4 and m=1/4
nodes.statement: The favour/suppress total-variation ratio is (5/18)/(5/42) = 7/3, and the one-gate edge-drift magnitude ratio is (5/72)/(5/168) = 7/3. The balanced conditional mutual information ratio is 0.023368444772049440 / 0.009748566529643857 = 2.397115996591876, which is not 7/3. Probability displacement and drift geometry share the linear ratio. Information geometry does not, because Jensen-Shannon divergence is nonlinear in the slot probabilities.

nodes.observable: minimal raw coordinates of the six-slot law
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: A formation and a dissolution of one slot, on the same triad literal with equal weights, give a law that reads only the gate. The slot's own bit is not a coordinate. All 16 such systems have one minimal coordinate and two rows: the slot carries m whenever the literal is true, in either edge state.

nodes.observable: scope of magnitude_class on the drift-direction inference
nodes.scope: Generation 8C drift-direction inference against the Generation 8 occupancy axis
nodes.statement: The large magnitude belongs to F010-OCCUPANCY-AXIS. F8C-DRIFT-DIRECTION explains the sign of that axis. The inference is a local direction and should not inherit the occupancy axis's magnitude classification.

nodes.observable: minimum triad bits determining the six-slot law given the full pair mask
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: Effective gate dimension is 0 on 16 systems, 1 on 960, and 2 on 2608. The local reducibility classes are R0 0, R1U 16, R1G 0, R1T 48, R2S 912, and R2G 2608. No R2G law matches any of the 433 one-rule comparator laws.

nodes.observable: I(full current triad ; next pair slot | full pair mask) across systems
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: The balanced current-triad slot information is constant on 80 groups defined by family, same or different triad, opposite literals on one triad, and the weight multiset. It does not change with vertex placement, action adjacency, action direction, or literal polarity. 3552 S4 local-law classes carry 57 distinct information values. The chain rule I(G1,G2) = I(G1) + I(G2 | G1) holds to 2.4e-15 on all 2608 two-gate systems, and a gate's information given the other gate is never below its marginal.

nodes.observable: balanced information against effective gate dimension and rule count
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: The largest balanced information in the census, 0.059365300578680294 nats, belongs to a dimension-one complementary two-level law, ORB-0101-W01. The dimension-two maximum is 0.04781829997118239 nats. A gated toggle, a slot-gate XOR, and a switched dimension-two system carry the same 0.046736889544 nats with one, two, and three coordinates. In 64 systems the two-rule information is below the larger single-rule value.

nodes.observable: log w(x,e) - (lambda1 phi1(x,e) + lambda2 phi2(x,e))
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: On every one of the 3584 weighted two-rule systems, the implementation kernel weights equal the product of the two rules' multipliers on all 1024 states as exact fractions. The combined log weight minus the sum of the two rules' log-weight features is at most 2.22e-16 on every state and pair slot. Each feature is the conjunction of the action's admissibility literal and one gate literal.

nodes.observable: logit interaction Delta12 L on the same action
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: On one action slot with two distinct gates, L11 - L10 - L01 + L00 = 0 on all 272 systems. The log multiplier is c + lambda1 l1(G1) + lambda2 l2(G2). The both-active level is fixed by the other three, no independent conjunction coefficient exists, and an XOR of two gate literals is not representable by two primitive one-gate rules under any choice of literals or weights. The nearest shape, L11 = L00, requires L10 = -L01.

nodes.observable: rule ablations against the full local law
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: In no weighted two-rule system does removing either rule leave the local law unchanged. The smallest maximum probability gap of any of the 10752 single-rule and empty ablations is 5/66. In the 16 complementary eliminations the gate bit is masked by equal weights, and each rule is still necessary.

nodes.observable: both-active six-slot law against the closed forms
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: When two rules on different slots are both active the pair law is m1/(m1+m2+4), m2/(m1+m2+4), and 1/(m1+m2+4) on the other four slots. When two rules on one slot are both active it is m1*m2/(m1*m2+5) and 1/(m1*m2+5). Both forms hold with exact-fraction gap 0 on every realised both-active state of 2480 different-action and 272 same-action systems. Opposite literals of one gate and opposite directions on one slot never activate both rules.

nodes.observable: labelled and S4 law hashes across structural orbits
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: On one slot the local law determines the affine log multiplier c + beta1 G1 + beta2 G2, not the literals that wrote it. Flipping both literals and inverting both weights leaves the law unchanged exactly when m1*m2 = 1. Sixteen labelled-law coincidences across orbits, and eight more under vertex permutation, are of this kind. With the eight complementary eliminations they are all of the cross-orbit coincidences: 24 labelled and 32 under S4.

nodes.observable: interpretation of the D0 grammar
nodes.scope: Generation 8D; not a claim about physical or biological systems
nodes.statement: Inside this model a small constraint grammar is compositional in event-logit space and bounded: two higher-order constraints can express a two-dimensional relational dependence that no single constraint expresses, and cannot express a relation between their two conditions. Visible dynamics come from normalisation, occupancy, and topology. A coherence account built on this grammar should attach meaning to the law, the affine logit and its placement, and not to the rule text.

nodes.observable: truth table of the six-slot law
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: A dissolution on one triad literal and a formation of the same slot on the opposite literal, with equal weights, make the action active exactly when the slot bit XOR the gate bit is 1. All 16 such systems have two coordinates and two rows. Two primitive rules realise an XOR between a slot's own bit and a gate bit, because each primitive feature already conjoins an admissibility literal with a gate literal.

nodes.observable: joint activation in the truth table and conditional gate information
nodes.scope: Generation 8D Round D0, all 3584 W4 weighted two-rule T->P systems at N=4, H=0, balanced weighting where information is named
nodes.statement: 256 of the 2608 dimension-two systems never activate both rules in one state. They are the opposite-direction pairs on one slot with two different triads. The pair mask selects which gate is read. Each needs two triad bits across masks and at most one at any mask. On exactly these 256 systems each gate's information given the other gate equals its marginal information. ORB-0028-W00 is the simplest named example, with two rows and information exactly twice the one-gate value.

nodes.observable: relation between rule syntax and local law
nodes.scope: two-rule T->P systems of Generation 8D Round D0
nodes.statement: Contextual syntax can be dynamically redundant. Complementary conditions with one weight remove the condition. Opposite directions on one literal with one weight remove the slot state. Reciprocal weights on flipped literals make two texts one kernel. The local law determines the affine logit, not the rule text.

nodes.observable: balanced CMI and rule-induced edge drift as functions of m

(1) E0's dense LU solve loses accuracy on improbable states: relative error up to 2.9e-6 at probability ~1e-12 (HELD N5, exact rational referee); in HELD N6 non-gradient cells it returned negative values that were clipped to exactly zero for 13-136 states per cell, so one_sided_transitions (published 120-2,136 in five cells) is an artefact (true value 0), and attachment_fraction_by_free_edge_count at densities of stationary mass 1e-14 to 1e-35 is wrong by up to 0.56. (2) E0's L1-stopped iteration in the saturated FREE N6 cells left states of mass 1e-33 to 1e-17 unconverged (relative error up to 1e15), so triangles_given_edge_count at those densities is noise. (3) edge_count_modes (strict peaks with exactly equal neighbours) and the 1e-15 inclusion threshold of top_net_currents depend on rounding. Every other published channel reproduces to 1e-10 absolute or 1e-8 relative in all 84 cells.

nodes.observable: CSPH attachment margin in four forms and two clocks; a/k profile; irreversible flux
nodes.scope: GT Round E1: HELD N=5,6,7 W4 and N=5,6 W3/W16, eight families, exact kernels (frozen plan 4ba2839)
nodes.statement: At HELD N=7 with the E0B W4 grades, CSPH's attachment margin over the size-specific null is at or below zero in every declared form and clock: raw -0.067 (continuous) and +0.002 (jump), ceiling-normalised -0.200 / +0.005, null-density-standardised -0.112 / -0.095, while its irreversible flux rises to 0.157. Basin-with-arrow coexistence (GT-F26) does not survive to N=7 in this family. Density-resolved, the preference for attachment survives at one or two free relations (a/k 0.718, 0.701 against r0 0.667) but is more negative at three to five than at N=6, and time at k<=2 falls 0.86 -> 0.68 -> 0.42; a post hoc decomposition attributes about one third of the N=6->7 loss to the occupied density profile and two thirds to the per-density preference.

nodes.observable: handover index (four steps, forward minus reverse), forward-step count, irreversible flux
nodes.scope: GT Round E1: HELD N=5,6,7 W4 and N=5,6 W3/W16, eight families, exact kernels (frozen plan 4ba2839)
nodes.statement: The handover orientation (probe-probe forms -> attachment forms -> probe-probe dissolves -> attachment dissolves) holds on all four adjacent steps in all 30 non-gradient E1 cells (six families x N=5,6,7 at W4 and N=5,6 at W3 and W16) and in none of the reversible controls. Irreversible flux is steady from N=6 to N=7 (0.14-0.16 in all six families); the per-event handover index is roughly constant with N for dissolution-acting rules and shrinks for formation-acting rules (PATHF 0.095 -> 0.076 -> 0.050).

nodes.observable: witness census: event share, mean engaged witnesses and log-weight per component (jump chain)
nodes.scope: GT Round E1: HELD N=5,6,7 W4 and N=5,6 W3/W16, eight families, exact kernels (frozen plan 4ba2839)
nodes.statement: From N=6 to N=7 the mean engaged log-weight of every non-gradient rule component on executed events changes by a factor 0.87-1.08, although the nominal path-witness maximum grows by 40/24 = 1.67 and the strengthening bracket scales log-weights by 1.585 (W3) and 2 (W16). The gradient closure control amplifies (1.35) because it fills the graph.

nodes.observable: C3 calibration, C4 N7 reading (17 declared channels), detachment, post hoc margin decomposition
nodes.scope: GT Round E1: HELD N=5,6,7 W4 and N=5,6 W3/W16, eight families, exact kernels (frozen plan 4ba2839)
nodes.statement: Uniform strengthening at fixed N is a poor quantitative proxy for growing N in this grammar. Doubling log-strength at N=5 reproduces the direction but not the size of the published N=5->6 step (frozen verdict: direction-only in five families, poor in CSPH; 0-6 of 17 channels comparable in size). The N=6->7 steps are mostly in the direction of strengthening at N=6 but smaller (55 of 102 channel readings), or opposite (22; probe-only hub share in all six families, near/far activity ratio in five). Strengthening raises detachment 0.52-0.55 -> 0.84-0.89 at N=6; growing to N=7 gives 0.55-0.58. Post hoc, strengthening acts almost entirely on the per-density preference with an occupancy part of opposite sign to that of growth in the dissolution-acting families.

nodes.observable: CSPH attachment margins and a/k profile by alphabet, both clocks
nodes.scope: GT Round E1: HELD N=5,6,7 W4 and N=5,6 W3/W16, eight families, exact kernels (frozen plan 4ba2839)
nodes.statement: In CSPH, strengthening at fixed N moves the two clocks' attachment margins in opposite directions: per event +0.065 -> +0.086 -> +0.092 (W4, W3, W16 at N=6) while per unit time +0.009 -> -0.110 -> -0.297; a/k at k=1-3 stays above the null per event (0.87, 0.91, 0.85) and falls below it per unit time (0.58, 0.65, 0.22). The same split holds at N=5. In CWPH and PATHH strengthening lowers both clocks' margins.

nodes.observable: CLOSEW margins (four forms), density, near/far activity ratio
nodes.scope: GT Round E1: HELD N=5,6,7 W4 and N=5,6 W3/W16, eight families, exact kernels (frozen plan 4ba2839)
nodes.statement: The reversible gradient control CLOSEW weak_favour is the only rule in E1 whose null-density-standardised attachment margin grows with N (+0.022, +0.034, +0.042 continuous); its raw margin falls to +0.0008 because density approaches the ceiling (0.81, 0.90, 0.96), and its near/far activity ratio falls 1.03 -> 0.89 -> 0.61 (near-source slowing grows with N). No arrow-carrying rule shows a size-stable standardised preference: all are -0.095 to -0.136 at N=7.

nodes.observable: detachment, detached-probe counts, autocorrelation times, equal-ratio class L1
nodes.scope: GT Round E1: HELD N=5,6,7 W4 and N=5,6 W3/W16, eight families, exact kernels (frozen plan 4ba2839)
nodes.statement: In every non-gradient family, probe detachment is size-stable (0.52-0.55 at N=6, 0.55-0.58 at N=7; NULL 0.018 at N=7), three or four of four probes are often detached together at N=7 (CSPH 0.49 per unit time), the correlation time of the attached-probe indicator in mean events grows with N (CSPH 4.6, 5.9, 7.0; PATHF 1.7, 3.1, 4.8), and the equal-ratio occupancy gap keeps growing but more slowly (class L1 N=5 0.18-0.22, N=6 0.32-0.49, N=7 0.37-0.62).

nodes.observable: inference from GT-F36, GT-F37, GT-F39, GT-F40
nodes.scope: GT Round E1: HELD N=5,6,7 W4 and N=5,6 W3/W16, eight families, exact kernels (frozen plan 4ba2839)
nodes.statement: In this grammar a stationary order of succession (the handover) and a time-weighted preference for relation to a held reference (attachment margin) are produced by the same non-gradient rules but are not coupled: from N=6 to N=7 the first is undiminished in every family while the second vanishes or stays negative in every form, and strengthening moves them independently (CSPH clock split). The margin itself factorises into a per-density preference and an occupied density profile, which size and strength load differently.

nodes.observable: interpretation of GT-F43
nodes.scope: GT Round E1: HELD N=5,6,7 W4 and N=5,6 W3/W16, eight families, exact kernels (frozen plan 4ba2839)
nodes.statement: RS reading (not a physical claim): the relational picture should keep succession (ordered actualisation, robust in this grammar) and gathering (time-weighted relation to a reference, fragile, density- and clock-dependent here) as distinct notions; evidence for one is not evidence for the other.

nodes.observable: signed square affinity census
nodes.scope: GT template grammar, any N, both clocks, positive factors
nodes.statement: Theorem (formal note section 2): in the ordinary pair-DSL template grammar with positive factors, the elementary square 'form e, form f, dissolve e, dissolve f' on slots e=(p,q), f=(p,r) from a base state x has log affinity sigma*(deg_x(r)-deg_x(q)), with sigma = sum of log factors of path_dissolve components minus those of path_form components; squares on disjoint slots have affinity 0; closure and adjacency components cancel. Verified on every intact square of all 64 E2 cells (residual <= 1e-15) and independently from the rule strings with exact fractions.

nodes.observable: partner-frame index, handover index, sigma
nodes.scope: GT Round E2A: N=5 HELD/FREE and HELD N=6, 21 rule combinations, exact kernels (frozen plan 1974678)
nodes.statement: The aggregated orientation (partner-frame index; HELD handover index) has the sign of sigma in every cell with sigma != 0, no one-way transitions and nonzero flux: 36 of 36 (32 in E2A including five grades, both modes, HELD N=6; 4 in E2B with a hard closure exclusion). Every E0/E1 family had sigma = +log 2, so E1's 30/30 invariance is the sigma>0 case. No aggregate proof is offered.

nodes.observable: handover and partner indices, flux, expected relations
nodes.scope: GT Round E2A: N=5 HELD/FREE and HELD N=6, 21 rule combinations, exact kernels (frozen plan 1974678)
nodes.statement: When sigma < 0 the handover reverses. Unsaturated, the reversal is plainly visible and, with adjacency suppression, comparable to forward handovers (0.015-0.19 at HELD N=5): adjacency-suppressed path_form weak_favour (ADPF) at HELD N=5 has handover index -0.112 and flux 0.152; hard closure exclusion plus a sigma<0 term gives -0.015 to -0.042 with flux 0.016-0.049. Every other sigma<0 cell saturates (10 of 10 relations) with reversed indices of 1e-13 to 4e-5.

nodes.observable: square circulation (sum of oriented edge currents) by role
nodes.scope: GT Round E2A: N=5 HELD/FREE and HELD N=6, 21 rule combinations, exact kernels (frozen plan 1974678)
nodes.statement: Local affinity does not fix local current: 6-36% of adjacent-square circulation runs counter to its square's affinity, up to 12% sits on adjacent squares without affinity, and oriented flow across zero-affinity disjoint squares reaches 35% of total flux (HELD N=6). The net oriented circulation on attachment/probe squares nevertheless has the sign of sigma in every HELD cell, including N=6 where 1,152 of 13,824 nonzero squares are locally reversed.

nodes.observable: matched dissolution: rate, normalisation, jump ratios, passage, precedence
nodes.scope: GT Round E2A: N=5 HELD/FREE and HELD N=6, 21 rule combinations, exact kernels (frozen plan 1974678)
nodes.statement: In soft rules the handover's release step is an opportunity (denominator) effect, not enabling: removing the probe-probe relation leaves the attachment's own dissolution rate unchanged (path_form rules) or lowers it (path_dissolve rules, log ratio -0.02 to -0.17), yet makes it the likelier next event (log +0.29 to +0.64) because a fast competing event is removed; passage within 8 events changes by <= 0.011. Across 288 soft groups: no strict enabling, opportunity larger than rate in 170, next-event change opposite to own-rate change in 54.

nodes.observable: strict enabling share, race committor, flux
nodes.scope: GT Round E2B: N=5 HELD/FREE, hard formation exclusions x weak path terms, exact kernels (frozen plan 9448f95)
nodes.statement: Strict enabling by dissolution occurs only with a hard component and is neither necessary nor sufficient for directed succession: hard closure exclusion alone (enabling up to 0.87) and hard adjacency exclusion (0.60) are reversible; hard closure exclusion plus a path term enables (0.72-0.98) with circulation following sigma; hard path-form exclusion enables (0.19 adjacent, 0.47 disjoint) with one-way release; every soft sigma!=0 cell circulates without strict enabling. An enabled event beats restoration of its support about half the time (0.49-0.53) against 0.00-0.28 with the support present.

nodes.observable: one-way flux, partner index, square census
nodes.scope: GT Round E2B: N=5 HELD/FREE, hard formation exclusions x weak path terms, exact kernels (frozen plan 9448f95)
nodes.statement: Hard path-form exclusion produces a directed mode of succession without cycle affinity: no intact square carries affinity, irreversibility is carried by one-way transitions that are all releases (re-formation forbidden while a two-path persists; 5.6-7.3% of flux), flux 0.17-0.26 at FREE N=5, and the partner index is positive (+0.070 to +0.126) whatever the added soft sigma, including sigma<0: a counterexample to sigma setting the orientation once one-way transitions exist.

nodes.observable: law identity across soft terms
nodes.scope: GT Round E2B: N=5 HELD/FREE, hard formation exclusions x weak path terms, exact kernels (frozen plan 9448f95)
nodes.statement: Theorem (formal note 5.3): under hard adjacency exclusion every reachable state is a matching, so no path witness can exist and any path term is inert; observed: five rules give one identical reversible law (flux 8e-16) with strict enabling 0.60. Hard exclusion of incidence removes the support on which non-gradient circulation acts.

nodes.observable: reachable class size
nodes.scope: GT Round E2B: N=5 HELD/FREE, hard formation exclusions x weak path terms, exact kernels (frozen plan 9448f95)
nodes.statement: Theorem (formal note 5.4): in HELD the source triangle supplies a two-path to every attachment slot and a neighbour to every source vertex, so hard path-form or adjacency exclusion forbids every attachment and HELD collapses to a two-state probe chain at N=5 (8 cells). The imposed reference is not neutral to hard rules.

nodes.observable: partner index, flux, recovery, partner split
nodes.scope: GT Round E3A: FREE N=4/5 and HELD N=5, path-formation ladder, hard against dissolution, controls, two scans (frozen plan ab5f341)
nodes.statement: Along path-formation factors 1/2, 1/4, 1/9, 1/16 and 0 (existing W4/W3/W16 grades and prohibit) the partner index (FREE N=5: 0.072, 0.104, 0.112, 0.111, 0.108), flux (0.11, 0.18, 0.21, 0.22, 0.23) and absence duration of witnessed releases (2.24, 2.82, 3.16, 3.27, 3.40) of the hard zero lie at the end of the soft ladder; only support topology is qualitatively new (one-way edges, gate distance ~2, direct recovery 0). Opposing dissolution down to soft sigma -log 16 lowers the hard mode's index (+0.070, +0.035, +0.007) without reversing it. Reading (not a theorem): the hard ban acts as sigma -> +infinity on witnessed formations, which restores agreement with sigma in every E2B/E3A cell.

nodes.observable: expected recovery time, direct-recovery share, gate distance
nodes.scope: GT Round E3A: FREE N=4/5 and HELD N=5, path-formation ladder, hard against dissolution, controls, two scans (frozen plan ab5f341)
nodes.statement: A relation released while path-witnessed stays absent longer than one released unwitnessed in every path-suppressing cell (hard FREE N=5: 3.40 vs 2.50 time units; soft 1/16: 3.27 vs 2.43; NULL: equal, 1.00). Two mechanisms separate by the direct-recovery share: gate-limited (hard: re-formation requires breaking a witness first, direct share 0, gate distance ~2) and rate-limited (soft: direct but slow, direct share 0.49 at 1/2 falling to 0.06 at 1/16). Saturated soft cells hold rare, long-lived holes (3,174 vs 112 time units).

nodes.observable: internal witness census; square affinity change under neutralisation
nodes.scope: GT Round E3B: HELD N=5/6, nine families on kernel and neutralised instrument kernel (frozen plan 1bc7c18)
nodes.statement: Theorem (formal note 7.4-7.5, derived after E3A, verified in all 18 E3B cells): in HELD every attachment slot has exactly two path witnesses lying wholly inside the source triangle, in every state (T7); a constant factor on all formations or dissolutions of one slot class changes no cycle affinity (T8). Hence each path component with factor m imposes an orientation-neutral occupancy bias m^2 on attachments: against attachment when its sigma contribution is positive. Visible in E3A: HELD attachment recovery ~16 and ~256 time units under factors 1/4 and 1/16.

nodes.observable: attachment margins (three forms, both clocks), detachment, handover index, flux: original versus neutralised
nodes.scope: GT Round E3B: HELD N=5/6, nine families on kernel and neutralised instrument kernel (frozen plan 1bc7c18)
nodes.statement: With the source-witness floor divided out of attachment rates (a counterfactual instrument kernel, not a grammar rule), every sigma>0 path family gathers above the size-specific null at HELD N=5 and 6 in the raw margin, both clocks (e.g. N=6 continuous: PATHF weak_suppress -0.206 -> +0.073; PATHH weak_favour -0.112 -> +0.128; CWPH -0.067 -> +0.153; CSPH +0.009 -> +0.177), detachment roughly halves (0.53 -> 0.27-0.40), and the handover keeps its orientation (index positive, smaller). The non-gathering of direction-carrying rules (GT-F18, GT-F36) is largely produced by the held triangle's own witnesses.

nodes.observable: partner index versus sigma on a factor grid
nodes.scope: GT Round E3A: FREE N=4/5 and HELD N=5, path-formation ladder, hard against dissolution, controls, two scans (frozen plan ab5f341)
nodes.statement: On frozen 9x9 grids of synthetic path-formation and path-dissolution factors (2^k, k in {-3,...,3} with half-steps), the partner index never disagreed in sign with sigma: FREE N=4 72 judged points, N=5 56 judged (16 below the 1e-12 floor at saturation). Evidence within the grid; no proof.

nodes.observable: partner-index split
nodes.scope: GT Round E3A: FREE N=4/5 and HELD N=5, path-formation ladder, hard against dissolution, controls, two scans (frozen plan ab5f341)
nodes.statement: Under hard path-formation exclusion with the strongest available opposing dissolution (W16), the part of the partner index carried by event pairs containing a one-way step is negative (N=4 -0.0026, N=5 -0.0006) while the two-way part is positive (+0.012, +0.0075); in the plain hard cell both parts are positive and comparable (N=5 +0.057, +0.051). Local one-way steps and aggregate circulation can run in opposite directions.

nodes.scope: GT Round E4B: HELD star K1,3 and path P4 x N=6 x six families (frozen plan 9a1c539)
nodes.statement: Within a held reference, new relations concentrate on its lowest-permanent-floor sites under every sigma>0 path family, both clocks, both sizes: P3 middle (floor 0) against ends (floor 1) about 2x (attachment per slot 0.29-0.37 against 0.14-0.22); star centre (floor 0) against leaves (floor 2) about 4x (0.36-0.37 against 0.085-0.093); uniform-floor P4 level for PATHF (0.146 against 0.155) with a smaller state-dependent inner preference under PATHH and CSPH (0.128/0.159, 0.092/0.151). Within-cell contrasts: source size, density, probes and null are held fixed. NULL and CLOSEW show no orbit difference.

nodes.observable: raw attachment margin against own null
nodes.scope: GT Round E4A: HELD K2/P3/K3 x N=5,6 x six families (frozen plan f5b3b50)
nodes.statement: Under a held single edge (K2, the only floor-free connected reference), every sigma>0 path family (PATHF ws, PATHH wf, CSPH) has attachment above its own NULL r0 = 2(N-2)/M in raw margins, both clocks, N=5 and 6 (+0.008 to +0.124), with unmodified label-covariant rules; the star K1,3 gives raw above-null attachment for PATHF and PATHH (+0.032 to +0.085). The handover keeps its orientation.

nodes.observable: standardised margins and overlap diagnostics
nodes.scope: GT Round E4A: HELD K2/P3/K3 x N=5,6 x six families (frozen plan f5b3b50)
nodes.statement: Null-density-standardised against each reference's own NULL profile, native raw gathering largely vanishes: K2 PATHF/PATHH -0.030 to +0.021, star -0.031 to -0.004; only CSPH under K2 stays positive in both clocks (N=5 +0.055/+0.068, N=6 +0.009/+0.031). At N=6, 18-31% of the NULL free-edge weight lies on low-mass counts, so the standardised form is partly counterfactual. Native gathering is mostly density composition, as GT-F34 found for CSPH under the triangle.

nodes.observable: raw margins at equal k, K, N
nodes.scope: GT Round E4B: HELD star K1,3 and path P4 x N=6 x six families (frozen plan 9a1c539)
nodes.statement: At equal source size, held-edge count and null (k=4, K=3, N=6, r0=8/12), the star (total floor 6, centre 0) gives raw above-null attachment for PATHF and PATHH (+0.059, +0.085 continuous) while the path P4 (total floor 4, uniform 1) is below null (-0.088, -0.077); CSPH is below null under both (-0.060, -0.251). P3 (floor-0 middle) stays slightly below null for PATHF/PATHH. The overall margin follows neither total floor nor the mere presence of a floor-free site.

nodes.observable: orbit attachment conditional on the chord; chord occupancy
nodes.scope: GT Round E4A: HELD K2/P3/K3 x N=5,6 x six families (frozen plan f5b3b50)
nodes.statement: The free P3 closing chord raises the middle's internal witnesses from 0 to 2; when it is present the middle's attachment collapses (PATHF N=5 0.411 -> 0.138; CSPH 0.539 -> 0.213) while the ends barely change; under sigma>0 path rules the held path suppresses the chord itself (occupancy 0.23-0.29 against 0.50 under NULL).

nodes.observable: handover index, flux
nodes.scope: GT Round E4B: HELD star K1,3 and path P4 x N=6 x six families (frozen plan 9a1c539)
nodes.statement: The handover keeps the E0 orientation in every sigma>0 cell under all five held references (K2, P3, K3, star, P4); its magnitude depends on the reference (CSPH N=5: K2 0.019, P3 0.018, K3 0.036; N=6 star 0.007, P4 0.011) while irreversible flux varies less (0.08-0.16).

nodes.observable: floor census
nodes.scope: GT Round E4B: HELD star K1,3 and path P4 x N=6 x six families (frozen plan 9a1c539)
nodes.statement: Theorems (docs/e4-formal-witness-floors.md): the permanent path-witness floor at source vertex s of any held graph H is the sum over held neighbours c of (deg_H(c) - 1) (F1); only K2 is floor-free among connected references (F2); per-slot state-independent formation/dissolution factors change no cycle affinity (F4, generalising E3 T8). Census-verified in all 48 E4 cells.

nodes.observable: stationary odds identity
nodes.scope: GT-P008 consolidation (no experiment): algebra, synthetic N=4 fixtures, post hoc views of E4 tables
nodes.statement: Theorems S1-S3: in any finite irreducible single-toggle chain whose rates do not read the toggled slot, occ/(1-occ) = E[F|x_e=0]/E[D|x_e=1]; under PATHF ws, PATHH wf and CSPH an attachment's stationary odds factor exactly as 2^(-floor(s)) times a residue that depends on the whole stationary law; the residue lies in [2^-W, 1] with W the dynamic template count (10-24 at N=5,6), so no local argument can sign the orbit ordering at E4 sizes.

nodes.observable: first-order orbit coefficients
nodes.scope: GT-P008 consolidation (no experiment): algebra, synthetic N=4 fixtures, post hoc views of E4 tables
nodes.statement: Theorem S4/S4b/S4c: at first order around the uniform law, d log odds/d eps = -E_0[w] for PATHF/PATHH, with E_0[w_(p,s)] = T/4 + K + floor(s)/4 + (N-7) deg_H(s)/4, so the within-reference index is floor + (7-N) held degree (CSPH: (9-N) with the degree term reversed by closure); held degree is a sorting channel of the same order as the floor; explicit connected held graphs (e.g. {01,02,03,12,14} at N=6) favour the higher-floor vertex at weak coupling (7 strict reversals, 41 ties among connected graphs on <= 5 vertices).

nodes.observable: continuous vs per-event orbit occupancy
nodes.scope: GT-P008 consolidation (no experiment): algebra, synthetic N=4 fixtures, post hoc views of E4 tables
nodes.statement: Theorems S2b, S5, S6: PCOMP's continuous-time law is uniform at any strength (no continuous sorting despite a floor) while its per-event law sorts (published +0.08 to +0.18 log odds); equal-ratio pairs (PATHF ws, PATHH wf) share their continuous law to first order, so their differences (GT-F17, P4 0.067 vs 0.255) are second order, while their per-event laws differ at first order.

nodes.observable: raw margin slope vs published margin
nodes.scope: GT-P008 consolidation (no experiment): algebra, synthetic N=4 fixtures, post hoc views of E4 tables
nodes.statement: Theorem S7/S7b: the raw-margin slope at eps=0 is (1/2M)[sum_A kappa - r0 sum_F kappa]; K3 N=5 (PATHF, PATHH) and P3 N=6 (PATHF) have strictly positive slopes but negative published margins at eps = ln 2 (-0.107, -0.044, -0.039), so these margins change sign in (0, ln 2): the triangle's stationary suppression is a finite-strength global effect, not a first-order consequence of its floor.

nodes.observable: orbit log-odds contrasts, sojourns, chord strata
nodes.scope: GT-P008 consolidation (no experiment): algebra, synthetic N=4 fixtures, post hoc views of E4 tables
nodes.statement: Post hoc on exposed E4 tables: the exact floor term is 71-100% of the continuous log-odds orbit contrast in P3 and the star for PATHF/PATHH/CSPH, with the residue reinforcing in 8 of 9 (P3 N=5 CSPH -0.003); the first-order index gives the continuous sign in 16/16 and the per-event sign in 19/20 within-reference contrasts (miss: P4 PATHF per event, -0.053 against +0.058); PATHF sorts only through formation (lifetime ratio 1), PATHH only through lifetime (waiting ratio 1); with the P3 chord present (equal internal witnesses) the middle's continuous advantage vanishes or reverses (-0.28 to -0.02).

nodes.observable: architecture
nodes.scope: GT-P008 consolidation (no experiment): algebra, synthetic N=4 fixtures, post hoc views of E4 tables
nodes.statement: Propositions R1-R3: in FREE label-covariant irreducible models the stationary law is invariant under all vertex permutations and every labelled vertex has identical long-run statistics; unbounded persistence of a labelled structure requires imposition, loss of irreducibility (frozen-in classes) or a diverging-lifetime limit; an emergent reference at finite N can therefore only be metastable, measured by a lifetime-to-turnover ratio against a matched-density null in each clock.

nodes.observable: methodological
nodes.scope: GT-P008 consolidation (no experiment): algebra, synthetic N=4 fixtures, post hoc views of E4 tables
nodes.statement: Within-cell orbit contrasts (GT-F60) are matched observations, not interventions on the floor: orbits also differ in held degree and dynamic witnesses (Q-1); chord-conditioned occupancies (GT-F64) are strata of one law, not chord interventions (Q-2); F4 covers cycle affinities only (Q-3); the P3 chord is suppressed under PATHF/PATHH (0.23-0.29) but not under CSPH (0.45-0.53) (Q-4).

nodes.observable: intact-motif episode lifetime, both clocks
nodes.scope: E5A (GT-P009): FREE N=5,6, six families, frozen plan 1dc43c6; target vs N0 vs ND; both clocks
nodes.statement: Intact motifs (I_TRI, I_STAR, I_2PATH) outlive the density-matched comparator ND in continuous time in 1/30 non-NULL rows (PATHH star, x1.004 at N=5, x1.093 at N=6); jump-clock lengths exceed ND in 22/30 but ND is not jump-density matched for those families. No intact motif persists through replacement of its own relations (T4: required-edge internal flux exactly 0 in all 24 laws).

nodes.observable: intact-motif CT lifetime
nodes.scope: E5A (GT-P009): FREE N=5,6, six families, frozen plan 1dc43c6; target vs N0 vs ND; both clocks
nodes.statement: Post hoc theorem: under a formation-only family (PATHF, CLOSEW) every present edge dissolves at rate 1, so an intact motif with r required edges has L_ct = 1/r exactly, independent of the rules' organisation; observed 1/3, 1/3, 1/2 for PATHF and CLOSEW at both N. CLOSEW intact rows are shorter than ND only because ND slows dissolution to match the dense profile.

nodes.observable: flexible episode lifetime and Omega

concepts.definition: Hard constraints change which transitions exist (support, reachable class, one-way transitions); soft constraints change positive rates. Zero lies outside the multiplicative/log-additive weight algebra, yet some stationary observables can be continuous along a ladder of soft factors ending at a hard ban.
concepts.label: Admissibility versus weighting
concepts.plain_definition: Forbidding something is different in kind from merely making it rare, even when the results sometimes look similar.

concepts.definition: GT and CL 8N both descend from CL 8G (22e252e) and share the constraint-lab DSL, kernel builder and coherence validator. Agreement on anything inherited is not independent evidence.

concepts.plain_definition: Two reports written with the same calculator can agree because of the calculator.

concepts.definition: A comparison process declared before results that matches a target on stated quantities (occupancy, density, mean rate, adjacent laws) so that remaining differences are attributable to what is not matched. Matching a quantity also fixes everything that quantity determines (e.g. Kac recurrence, CT edge lifetime).
concepts.label: Matched-control design
concepts.plain_definition: A fair comparison keeps chosen things equal on purpose, and you must know what else that silently keeps equal.

concepts.definition: A conclusion about a stochastic relational process can change with the time parameterisation (continuous time vs jump/event count vs an epoch counting only some event types) and with the projection used to read it out. The clock is part of the estimand.
concepts.label: Clock and readout dependence
concepts.plain_definition: What you see depends on how you count time and what you choose to watch.

concepts.definition: Five distinct estimands that are easily conflated: occupancy (one-time stationary mass), passage (hitting/committor/first-passage between declared sets), retention (survival of a configuration or memory), resilience (return after perturbation) and reconstruction (recovery of a configuration after loss). Each needs its own declared source law, clock and control.
concepts.label: Retention, resilience, reconstruction, occupancy and passage
concepts.plain_definition: How common something is, how you reach it, how long it lasts, whether it bounces back and whether it can be rebuilt are five different questions.

concepts.definition: Dependence of a lower-order event (a pair toggle) on higher-order current structure: triads, paths, witness counts or hyperedges. Distinct from history and from initial-condition memory.
concepts.label: Higher-order and topological context
concepts.plain_definition: Whether one link changes can depend on the shape of the links around it.

concepts.definition: Long-lived memory of an initial condition or past selection (retention, which decays in an irreducible chain) is distinct from exact dependence of the next event on current structure.
concepts.label: Retention versus current dependence
concepts.plain_definition: Forgetting where you started is not the same as ignoring where you are now.

concepts.definition: Whether some record of past events must be added to the current state to predict the future (Markov sufficiency on an augmented state), as distinct from history merely being informative about the past. Includes the compilation question: can a fixed current-state kernel reproduce the history-conditioned law?
concepts.label: History as a predictive variable
concepts.plain_definition: Sometimes the present snapshot is enough to predict what comes next; sometimes you also need to know how you got here.

concepts.definition: Two finite Markov processes can share a one-time stationary law (or a matched stationary occupancy) yet differ in multi-time statistics: passage and first-passage times, episode lifetimes, two-step laws or order. Quantities fixed by the stationary law alone (e.g. Kac set recurrence 1/pi(D)) cannot discriminate them.
concepts.label: Occupancy does not fix process
concepts.plain_definition: Knowing how often something is the case does not tell you how long it lasts or how it gets there.

concepts.definition: A state description (or quotient of it) is predictively sufficient for a declared observable and horizon if conditioning on it renders further past information irrelevant to that observable's future law. Valid dynamical quotients must commute with the kernel (strong lumpability).
concepts.label: Future-relative predictive sufficiency
concepts.plain_definition: A summary is good enough when adding more detail about the present or past would not improve your forecast of the thing you care about.

concepts.definition: A stationary chain is reversible iff detailed balance holds (no net cycle currents); a stationary arrow is net irreversible flux. Which rule classes guarantee reversibility depends on label covariance and witness structure.
concepts.label: Reversibility and stationary arrow
concepts.plain_definition: A process has a direction when, even in balance, it runs around some loops more one way than the other.

concepts.definition: An object chosen by an observer for an extreme current property (e.g. the maximum-degree vertex) shows that property at selection time by construction; persistence is the decay of that advantage under the dynamics, against comparators. In finite exchangeable irreducible chains no labelled object stays distinguished.
concepts.label: Selection is not persistence
concepts.plain_definition: Picking the tallest person in a room does not show that tallness lasts.

concepts.definition: Gravitational attraction as understood in physics. Not a model object in any programme here. It is named only so that tempting but unsupported bridges (false attractors) can be recorded and rejected.
concepts.label: Physical gravitational attraction (external notion)
concepts.plain_definition: Gravity as physicists mean it, which none of these models derives.
